steps.text: Inspect hillsides around your home for fresh cracks or tilting trees.
Monitor hillside water drainage channels for sudden muddy runoff or blockages.
Prepare an evacuation backpack with dry food and prescription medicines.
Identify safe shelter locations away from steep slopes and ravines.
Keep battery torches and spare batteries ready in accessible places.
Stay alert during prolonged heavy rainfall, especially during night hours.
Agree on an emergency family meeting place on stable flat ground.
Save local district control room numbers on your phone.
Evacuate immediately if you hear loud rumbling or cracking sounds.
Move sideways away from the path of mud and falling rocks.
Never cross or walk through an active debris flow.
Avoid river valleys and low ravines where debris flows concentrate.
Curl into a tight ball and protect your head if trapped.
Call 112 as soon as you reach stable flat ground.
Warn neighbors along the slope by shouting or blowing whistles.
Do not stop on bridges or under steep road embankments.
Stay away from slide areas; secondary landslides often occur quickly.
Check for injured or trapped neighbors without entering unstable ground.
Report broken utility lines and damaged gas connections immediately.
Check your building foundation and chimney for fresh structural cracks.
Replant damaged ground promptly to reduce risk of future erosion.
Do not drink tap water until authorities declare supplies uncontaminated.
Listen to local radio advisories regarding highway and pass openings.
Follow instructions from district rescue personnel and NDRF teams.
